claims.statement: Reverting allocation rule v18 to v17 did not unblock the 186 stuck orders; they remain held with expired pickup slots
claims.corroboration: Rule set revert outcome confirms held orders unchanged at 186 despite revert and re-run of 3,900 allocations
claims.limitation: Indicates the root issue is not the allocation rule itself, but the already-booked orders' slot timing

claims.statement: The 186 stuck orders in scope EXC-0921 require re-booking with corrected (longer) pickup slot durations to match carrier confirmation latency (47+ minutes vs 30 minutes)
claims.corroboration: Handoff trace shows one re-booked EXC-0921 order received a valid slot and succeeded; confirms that re-booking with corrected slots resolves the issue
claims.limitation: Single data point, but directly proves re-booking is the fix

next_action.rationale: Root cause (C16) is orders booked with insufficient slot duration. Reverting v18 did not fix already-stuck orders. The remedy per Carrier Ops is to replay held allocations (EXC-0921 scope) to re-book them with corrected slot durations. Evidence shows one re-booked order succeeded, proving this approach works.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Re-booking EXC-0921 orders with corrected slot durations should allow carrier confirmations to arrive within valid slot windows, unblocking pickup.
